concept: Mode collapse and typicality bias in preference tuning
summary: Source-anchored research for Mode collapse and typicality bias in preference tuning. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Post-training methods sharpen the output probability distribution and reduce diversity of generated responses; DivPO counters this by picking rarer, higher-quality responses as preferred and common lower-quality ones as rejected, reporting +45.6% persona attribute diversity and +74.6% story diversity with comparable quality. (medium confidence)

Verbalized Sampling, a training-free prompt asking the model to verbalize a distribution of responses with probabilities, reports 1.6-2.1x diversity gains in creative writing, with larger gains for more capable models. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-15)

RLHF significantly reduces output diversity compared with SFT across several measures, while generalising better out of distribution; the authors frame this as a generalisation-diversity tradeoff (tested on two base models, summarisation and instruction following). (high confidence)

Verbalized Sampling paper identifies typicality bias in preference data (annotators systematically favour familiar text) as a data-level driver of mode collapse, formalised theoretically and checked on preference datasets; it claims collapse occurs even with a perfect reward model. (medium confidence)

Aligned (RLHF) Llama-2 models show lower token-prediction entropy, distinct clusters in embedding space, and 'attractor states', indicating constrained diversity; study covers only the Llama-2 family. (medium confidence)
